synopsis: The ISO 18497:2024 agricultural series, published in July 2024, is identified as the closest published cousin of heavy off-road collision mitigation, covering obstacle protection and verification/validation, including braking, steering and person or obstacle detection tests [f7187, f15283, f7188, f1711]. ISO 18497-4 explicitly lists simulation among several verification methods and supplies simulation test objects, but the research found neither a defined virtual-evidence share nor authorization to replace field tests with simulation [f9764, f5276, f1954, f15288]. Its premise that detection is imperfect yields four failure categories—failure to detect, late detection, incorrect classification and localization error—which the booklet recommends using with ISO 21815-3 risk areas to structure the scenario catalogue [f15285, f15289]. IEC 61496 and IEC TS 62998 offer a component-level sensor certification basis, but IEC TS 61496-5:2023 excludes aspects of moving radar protective-device applications; certification therefore does not establish whole-machine performance in dust and rain, and mobile outdoor use of IEC TS 62998-1 is presented as a vendor claim [f1038, f12393, f15280, f1045]. No simulation wording was found in ISO 3691-4:2023, which is described as current and under revision with an Edition 3 DIS in progress [f9784, f9783]. These positive findings coexist with chapters saying that ISO 18497 details or simulation provisions, and ISO 3691-4 provisions, were not verified, so editions and clauses require checking before reliance [f4335, f7741, f11198].
